**EM alternates between soft cluster assignments and weighted parameter fitting.** In a Gaussian mixture, the component responsible for each observation is hidden. The E-step computes its posterior probability under the current parameters; the M-step treats those responsibilities as fractional memberships. [1](https://probml.github.io/pml-book/book1.html) [2](https://probml.github.io/pml-book/book2.html)

If one point has responsibilities (0.8,0.2), it contributes 0.8 of an observation to the first component and 0.2 to the second. Summing those fractions gives effective component counts. Weighted means and variances then update each Gaussian, while normalized counts update mixture probabilities.

**Use the new mean when recomputing variance.** Otherwise the update does not match the stated M-step. Compute responsibilities in log space to avoid underflow when densities are tiny.

Exact EM does not decrease the likelihood, but that does not guarantee the best global mixture. A component can collapse onto one point with vanishing variance, creating a singular likelihood. Use variance floors or priors, multiple initializations, and a policy for tiny components. Inspect likelihood improvement and component behavior together rather than calling any monotonic training curve a valid density estimate.

**Technical details and references.**

For $p(x_i)=\sum_k\pi_k\mathcal N(x_i;\mu_k,\sigma_k^2)$, the E-step computes responsibilities $r_{ik}=\pi_k\mathcal N(x_i;\mu_k,\sigma_k^2)/\sum_j\pi_j\mathcal N(x_i;\mu_j,\sigma_j^2)$. With $N_k=\sum_i r_{ik}$, the M-step sets $\pi_k=N_k/N$, $\mu_k=\sum_i r_{ik}x_i/N_k$, and $\sigma_k^2=\sum_i r_{ik}(x_i-\mu_k)^2/N_k$. [1](https://probml.github.io/pml-book/book1.html) [2](https://probml.github.io/pml-book/book2.html)

Use the newly updated mean in the variance step and stable log probabilities for responsibilities. Exact EM does not decrease likelihood, but may converge to a local optimum and can encounter a singular component collapsing onto one observation. Use multiple initializations, covariance floors or priors, and a defined policy for tiny/empty components. Stop using likelihood improvement plus parameter diagnostics, not a fixed iteration count alone.
